summary: Thinley Dorji Bhutia works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as Tibetan Teacher and Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School, Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1994), and Chief Editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1994).

Thinley Norbu Rinpoche (1931–2011) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Mindrolling Monastery and under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (Dudjom Rinpoche), and he founded the White Lotus School.

Thomas A. Forsthoefel is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned a B.A. from Georgetown University, an M.A. from Loyola University Chicago, and a Ph.D. from the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths, later serving at Mercyhurst University.

Thomas A. Tweed (born 1954) is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at Stanford University (~1980–1984) under William R. Hutchison, and served as Professor of Religious Studies at UNC Chapel Hill (~1993–2008).

Thomas B. Ellis is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania and served as Assistant Professor of Religion in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at Appalachian State University (attested 2009).

Thomas Berry (1914–2009) worked in religious studies, Sinology, and Indology. He studied at the Catholic University of America (~1944–1948) and held posts at the City University of New York and Fordham University (~1966–1979).

Thomas Borchert is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral candidacy at the University of Chicago (attested 2005). As of 2017, he was Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont.

Thomas Burrow (1909–1986) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Christ's College, Cambridge, SOAS, and Annamalai University. He served as Assistant Keeper at the British Museum and Boden Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Oxford (1944–1976).

Thomas Christian Tychsen (1758–1834) was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Kiel University (~1777–1779) and the University of Göttingen (~1779–1781), where he later held a post from ~1784 to 1834.

Thomas Cleary (1949–2021) worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied under E. Bruce Brooks, earned a Ph.D. from Harvard University (~1970–1975), and received a J.D. from the University of California, Berkeley.

Thomas Doctor is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and the University of Lausanne, supervised by Christian K. Wedemeyer for his MA and Tom Tillemans for his doctoral research.

Thomas E. Crow (born 1948) studied at Pomona College and UCLA. He taught at CalArts, Chicago, Princeton, Michigan, Sussex, Yale, and USC, served as director of the Getty Research Institute (2000–2007), and became Rosalie Solow Professor at NYU in 2007.

Thomas Edward Colebrooke (1813–1890) was an Indologist who studied at Eton College and East India Company College. He served as President (1864–1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

Thomas Freeman Yarnall works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington and Columbia University (Ph.D. by 2003 under Robert A. F. Thurman), where he became Executive Editor in the Department of Religion (attested 2007).

Thomas Henry Huxley (1825–1895) studied at Great Ealing School, University College London, and Charing Cross Hospital Medical School (~1842–1845). He held a post at Imperial College London from ~1854 to 1885.

Thomas J. Mazanec is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Calvin University and the University of Colorado (MA), and completed doctoral work under supervisors Anna M. Shields, Stephen F. Teiser, and doctoral advisor Wang Ping.

Thomas Jólch (born 1975) is a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Frankfurt, Hull (MA), Heidelberg, and Munich (PhD ~2005–2011). He worked as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University from 2013 to 2019.

Thomas Nathan Patton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under Anne M. Blackburn and earned his Ph.D. at Cornell University, later holding a post at the City University of Hong Kong (attested 2018).
Thomas Oberlies is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied under Albrecht Wezler and Paul Thieme, and held a post at the University of Freiburg (attested 2001).

Thomas P. Kasulis (born 1948) is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He held academic posts at Ashland University (~1980–1991) and Ohio State University (~1991–2016), where he served as Professor.
